page: Microsoft Azure M64s is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. It also includes 2097 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not feature any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates a clear trade-off between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 10%, reflecting lower single-threaded execution speeds. However, multi-core capabilities are robust, with stress-ng multi-core performance and Geekbench multi-core scores ranking in the middle 50%. Notably, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression both rank in the top 25%, demonstrating strong data throughput capabilities when utilizing parallel processing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M64s offers high memory density and substantial local storage capacity, making it a viable option for workloads that require massive RAM allocations rather than raw single-threaded compute power. The instance is well-suited for memory-intensive enterprise applications, large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and multi-threaded data decompression or batch processing pipelines.
description: The Microsoft Azure M64s is a memory-optimized server instance designed for resource-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, paired with 1024.0 GB of RAM and 2097 GB of local storage. While single-core benchmarks place the instance in the bottom 10%, its multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities are highly competitive, with large-block memory read speeds and multi-threaded decompression performance ranking in the top 25%. This hardware profile offers high memory density, making it qualitatively cost-effective for memory-bound applications rather than compute-heavy single-threaded tasks. The M64s is highly suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching, and parallelized data processing workloads.
